verdicts.summary: Thread path: the marker cannot pass earlier batches. On overflow, the stream fails and the producer stops. The pre-delivery build-up is the same hazard as the shell one I added below, but it is far less likely here: only one thread's events are buffered, and tool updates are coalesced every 50ms while waiting.
verdicts.scenario: Tried two cases. (1) A marker is offered while a batch from PubSub is still being coalesced. (2) The budget overflows while the window fiber is flushing. In (1), offerAll holds the mutex for the whole batch, and flushPending runs before the marker is retained and offered. In (2), the window fiber swallows the error, the forked close takes the mutex, then clears and fails the output. deliver races `failed`, so a pull blocked on the queue ends.

verdicts.summary: Shell raw events are charged to the budget from subscribe time, but nothing coalesces or drains them until delivery begins. Delivery begins only after the snapshot or the catch-up replay has been sent and ACKed. The 1,000-item limit therefore counts raw events from all threads that arrive during that phase. On a busy server, a slow client overflows, resubscribes, and overflows again on every retry, so it never synchronizes.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Several threads are streaming message deltas or activity appends; the comment at ws.ts:1400-1402 calls these high-frequency bursts. 2) A slow client calls subscribeShell, with or without afterSequence. 3) From ws.ts:1434 every domain event is retained raw (ws.ts:1437). Nothing pulls liveBuffer while loadSnapshot runs and while the snapshot or the up-to-1,000-event catch-up (ws.ts:1517/1537) waits for client ACKs. groupedWithin and replace only run once synchronizedThenLive is pulled. 4) More than 1,000 events arrive in that time, so LiveStreamBudget.ts:87 calls overflow and the stream fails. 5) The client retries after 250ms. The gap is now above 1,000 (SHELL_RESUME_MAX_GAP, ws.ts:334), so it takes the snapshot path, which reloads and resends the whole snapshot and starts the same race. Before this commit the queue was unbounded and the client eventually caught up.
verdicts.consequence: A slow client on a busy server repeatedly errors and resubscribes, downloading the full shell snapshot on every retry. Its shell list never goes live, and server load from repeated snapshots goes up.
verdicts.missing: The real event rates and snapshot transfer times, which are runtime behaviour I cannot read. The sequence of steps itself is allowed by the code.

verdicts.summary: offerAll, flushWindow and close all take one mutex, and flushWindow checks the generation again after it gets the permit. cancelWindow can only interrupt a window fiber that is sleeping or waiting for the mutex, never one inside flushPending. I found no deadlock and no double flush.
verdicts.scenario: Tried two cases. (1) close or offerAll calls cancelWindow while the window fiber is waiting for the mutex. Interrupting a fiber that is waiting for a permit returns normally. (2) The window fiber overflows inside flushPending, and the forked close waits on the mutex. The failing fiber returns its error and releases the permit first. Its ensuring step does not touch windowFiber, because close has already bumped the generation.
